reconstructed_theorem_text:
Let E and S be types. E has a normed additive commutative group structure, a real inner product space structure, is complete and finite dimensional over the reals, and has a measurable space structure equal to its Borel structure; S has an arbitrary measurable space structure. Let V:E→R and κ∈R. Assume κ≥1, V is twice continuously Frechet differentiable over R, and for every x,v∈E, κ^{-1}||v||^2 ≤ D(DV)(x)[v][v] ≤ ||v||^2. Let eta:S→R and y:S→E be measurable, with eta(s)>0 for every s∈S.
There exists one measurable p:S→E satisfying p(s)+eta(s)∇V(p(s))=y(s) for every s∈S. For this p define, for s∈S and u∈E, rho(s,u)=V(p(s)+sqrt(eta(s))u)-V(p(s))-sqrt(eta(s))<∇V(p(s)),u>_R and Q(s,u)=||u||^2/2+rho(s,u). Define mu=volume.tilted(x↦-V(x)), R(s)=mu.tilted(x↦-||x-y(s)||^2/(2 eta(s))), and r(s) as the pushforward of R(s) under x↦sqrt(eta(s))^{-1}(x-p(s)), where real-vector multiplication is scalar multiplication. For a measure nu and real function f, nu.tilted(f) literally means nu.withDensity(x↦ENNReal.ofReal(exp(f(x))/(∫exp(f)dnu))); the real Bochner normalization is totalized if integrability fails.
The measure mu is a probability measure. Moreover, for every s∈S, all the following hold simultaneously: R(s) is a probability measure; rho(s,·) and Q(s,·) are twice continuously Frechet differentiable over R; ∇rho(s,·)(0)=0 and ∇Q(s,·)(0)=0; for every u,v∈E, 0≤D(D(rho(s,·)))(u)[v][v]≤eta(s)||v||^2; for every u,v∈E, ||v||^2≤D(D(Q(s,·)))(u)[v][v]≤(1+eta(s))||v||^2; r(s)=volume.tilted(u↦-Q(s,u)); r(s) is a probability measure; the identity map on E belongs to L2(r(s)); u↦||u||^2 is integrable with respect to r(s); ∫||u||^2 dr(s)≤dim_R(E); the function u↦∇rho(s,·)(u) belongs to L2(r(s)); ∫||∇rho(s,·)(u)||^2 dr(s)≤eta(s)^2∫||u||^2 dr(s); and ∫||∇rho(s,·)(u)||^2 dr(s)≤eta(s)^2 dim_R(E).
Here volume is the finite real Hilbert Lebesgue/Haar measure, dim_R(E) is the actual real finite dimension interpreted as a real number in the inequalities, and all Hessians and gradients are actual Frechet/Riesz objects. Membership in L2 includes almost-everywhere strong measurability and finiteness of the L2 norm. Every point and direction quantified above ranges over all E. The construction uses a single p; mu's probability assertion precedes the universal quantifier over s. There is no eta upper bound, no nonzero-dimension assumption, no asserted uniqueness of p, and no conclusion of joint measurability of s↦R(s) or s↦r(s). R(s) is the literal conditional Gibbs tilt and r(s) its centered and sqrt(eta(s))-standardized law. Equality to a tilted measure is accompanied by separate probability assertions; it is not itself interpreted as establishing probability.
